newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FOCUS - Waterford Wedgwood in Rosenthal stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Waterford Wedgwood in Rosenthal stake.

text.p: Irish crystal and china firm Waterford Wedgwood Plc said on Thursday it was taking a 9.1 percent stake in Rosenthal AG as part of a strategic alliance with the German porcelain firm.

It said it had options to acquire a further 15 percent of Rosenthal over the next four years. The initial 9.1 percent stake would be acquired through the issue of 60,000 new Rosenthal shares at or close to the market price.

The company gave no indication of how much it expected to pay for the stake but Irish analysts said that based on Rosenthal's current share price, Waterford Wedgwood would pay around 2.5 million punts ($4.2 million).

The alliance between two of the world's famous names in porcelain would improve joint penetration of the German and British markets and foster improved overseas sales for Rosenthal, Waterford Wedgwood said.
Collaboration in manufacturing would further enhance profitability, it added.
"This is an outstanding opportunity to forge a true strategic alliance with another of the world's great tabletop companies," Waterford Wedgwood Chairman Tony O'Reilly said.

O'Reilly, one of Ireland's most famous businessmen through his chairmanship of H.J. Heinz Co and interests in several Irish companies, said the alliance would turn around the fortunes of the loss-making German firm.
"I am sure that, together, we can restore the fortunes of Rosenthal to the benefit of employees and shareholders alike, as Waterford Wedgwood continues to grow in the luxury brand business," he said.
Speculation about Waterford Wedgwood's interest in Rosenthal was sparked in June by a report in Germany's Focus magazine which said the Irish firm wanted to take over Rosenthal.
On Wednesday, Rosenthal said Waterford Wedgwood would be taking a stake and said it would propose to shareholders that regulations capping their voting rights should be scrapped.
Individual shareholders can currently command a maximum vote of five percent, even if their shareholding is larger than this.
"Rosenthal is a lovely fit for Wedgwood," said Joe Burnell, equity analysts at Davy Stockbrokers.

"It's a fine brand but it doesn't have many sales outside Europe. Conversely, Wedgwood doesn't have many sales in mainland Europe. So the two will be able to complement each other on that score," he said.
Burnell said Waterford Wedgwood's influence would be good for Rosenthal but he did not see the Irish firm making an early move to take over the whole company.
"Waterford Wedgwood are approaching this cautiously, rather than going hell-for-leather into a business which has been loss-making and may need some restructuring," he said.
